title: Status of Agriculture in India, Farming Systems and Livelihoods
shortDescription: Where Indian agriculture stands today, traditional vs modern farming systems and what a farming system consists of.
genZNote: Agriculture isn't just crops — it's soil, water, animals, markets and people all in one system. Think ecosystem, not field.

sections.heading: Status of Agriculture
bullets: Agriculture and allied sectors employ roughly 45% of India's workforce and contribute about 15–18% of GVA (check the latest Economic Survey).
India is a leading producer of milk, pulses, spices, jute, and the second largest producer of rice, wheat, fruits, vegetables and cotton.
Challenges: small and fragmented holdings (average ~1.1 ha), monsoon dependence, soil degradation, water stress, price volatility and post-harvest losses.
Policy anchors: MSP, PM-KISAN, PMFBY crop insurance, e-NAM, Soil Health Card, PMKSY irrigation, FPO scheme, Digital Agriculture Mission.

table.caption: Farming systems
rows: Slash-and-burn in hill/tribal regions, short cultivation, long fallow
Biological inputs; zero-budget natural farming promoted in Gujarat and elsewhere
Sensors/GPS, minimum tillage, residue retention, crop rotation

sections.heading: Components and Livelihood Systems
bullets: Components of a farming system: soil, water, crops, livestock, trees/horticulture, fisheries, labour, capital, technology and markets; interactions create nutrient recycling and risk spreading.
Farming-based livelihood systems: crop production, dairying, poultry, goat rearing, fish farming, agroforestry, processing and marketing; seasonal pluriactivity and off-farm income.
Sustainability: soil health, water-use efficiency, diversification, climate-smart practices.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Indian agriculture combines traditional and modern farming systems; farming systems integrate crops, livestock and allied enterprises to sustain rural livelihoods.
keyFacts: e-NAM, PMFBY, PM-KISAN are core schemes.

commonTraps: Do not equate shifting cultivation with commercial farming.

sources.name: Economic Survey of India — Agriculture chapter
